stem:
Tara observes human cells under a microscope. One cell is very long and thin, with thread-like branches. She knows nerve cells carry messages, cheek cells form a protective lining, and muscle cells help move food.

Which statement best explains how this long, branched shape helps the cell?

options.text: The long, branched shape helps the nerve cell carry messages over long distances.
The long, branched shape forms because carrying messages stretches the cell.
Cheek cells and nerve cells in the same person have this same long, branched shape.
The long, branched shape helps the cell move food.

teacher.key_rationale: A long, branched nerve cell is suited to carrying messages over long distances. Stretching is not what creates the shape; cheek cells are not shaped like nerve cells; length alone does not mean the cell moves food.

mx_swap.reason: Contracting-to-push-messages CWO needs a contraction claim not parallel to the shape-function frame; kept relationship_reversal, scope_error, and surface_feature_capture.
